name: BaboonLock
description: The BaboonLock is our go-to webbing anchor. Solidly built and rigourously tested, this versatile webbing anchor is a must for every slackliner.

name: BANANA! 3.0 SR
description: Lightweight and compact webbing anchor device. Small dimensions and low weight makes it perfect all-rounder. Equipped with movable captive front pin for fast and simple webbing installation with no chance of loosing the pin. Great care was taken to ensure no sharp edges remains, to avoid the risk of webbing abrasion or damage. Permanent riveting makes all elements the solid unity.

Great care was taken to ensure no sharp edges remains, to avoid the risk of webbing abrasion or damage. Permanent riveting makes all elements the solid unity.

name: Canon FX
description: A weblock so strong it hurt a lab member’s of staff ego while trying to tear it apart. Oh, and unlike the unharmed weblock, the pull tester had to be fixed.

unmodelled.full_name: Cat on slack Catlock SR PRO

name: Equilocker
description: The Equilocker by Sigma Slacklines - the high-quality longline linelock for 25 mm slacklines. Thanks to its generous dimensions it also takes thick webbing or doubled slacklines. Direct connection to 12 mm stainless steel shackles or 2 t steel shackles, no loops or slings needed. The front pin (12 mm, freely rotating) allows comfortable pre-tensioning by hand. The large central redirect made of anodised 7075 aluminium ensures maximum use of the breaking strength. Framed by 4 mm thick, deburred and glass-bead-blasted stainless steel plates.

name: Frog
description: The Frog is the first webbing anchor in high-strength stainless steel, very lightweight for a MBS of 60 kN, compatible with all connectors from 8 mm to 20 mm and even with slings. And the shape of the main diverter allows you to use your webbing to 98% of its strength.

name: Ginkgo
description: The Ginkgo is a trickline anchor, built to be extra strength solid, with a MBS of 100 kN, it is aimed at all those who want to pull off high amplitude tricks without fear. This has been designed and built to be the highest breaking strength webbing anchor on the market. Intended for webbings of between 40 – 50 mm, it has (WLL) of 00 kN, a 30 mm central diverter and a 16 mm steel front bolt pin

name: Katana FX
description: Katana is a cutting-edge piece for the most immense tricks and flights. When partnered with EQB Ninja line, it will take you to another trickline level.

name: KingPin Weblock
description: The KingPin Weblock is high-tech solution for 20mm slackline webbings. It is super light, has a high breaking load efficiency and allows you to pre-tension the line.

name: Lime
description:
Designed and produced entirely in Italy by Spider Slackline. Lime line lock is developed to be versatile with any type of connector, light and resistant with a working load up to 12kN. A line lock is essential for tensioning slacklines longer than 50 meters.

Note: Based on the design from EQB, the Lime is a rebranded version of the [Bandit SH](/weblocks/13).

name: LineLock AL MK4
description: The lineLock AL was first introduced in 2012 and is still today one of the smallest and lightest longline compliant slackline anchoring devices on the market.

name: Linelocker
description: The simplest and lightest weblock on the market. Classic linelocker that is used for slackline rigging for more than 10 years now. Ultralight aluminium version weighs only 24 grams!

name: Lynx 2.1
colors: blue side plates, gold roller ("blue jewel")
description:
Our Lynx embodies elegance and lightness paired with powerful strength and sophisticated functionality. The main application field are slackline setups up to 100m length and 12 kN preload.

The slackline can be fixed very fast and conveniently with the Lynx, now in the updated version 2.1. The possibility of pretighten the slackline with the hand gives superior precision and control while using rope pulley systems as tighteners. Thus, the static rope is used at maximum efficiency. Naturally, the Lynx 2.1 ensures a low strength reduction of the webbing.
notes: date_introduced cleared: the SlackDB value (Jan 2011) predates Landcruising's own Lynx 2.0 release post (1 Dec 2011), and 2.1 is the later revision of 2.0.

name: Lynx 3.0
description:
The newly developed and completely revised 3rd generation of our classic webbing anchor comes up with new highlights and innovations.

The optimized strength to weight ratio makes the Lynx 3.0 to the absolute allrounder amongst webbing anchors.

The direct fit to the compact and highly secure Green Pin shackles (1.5 To WLL and 2 To WLL) ensures a consistently high safety standard and a great long-term fatigue resistance in slackline anchors and setups. The large rear connection hole in combination with the universal width allows for the use of the common stainless steel shackles.

The new push button front pin made from high strength stainless steel provides safe anchorage due to the high pullout resistance. The quick-release design enables fast and gentle installing and removing of the webbing.

The new larger middle diverter with an outer diameter of 28 mm increases the breaking efficiency of every webbing. The diverter is now equipped with the innovative R-Lock principle. R-Lock effectively prevents any rotation of the diverter under very high shock loads, thus minimizing the risk of webbing slippage under extreme loading.

The new spacious design of the side plates ensures the excellent guidance of very thick webbings (e.g. threaded lines) or double layup techniques (double line training).

name: Lynx 4.0 SH
description:
Innovative 25 mm allround weblock for direct attachment to various shackles and connection components. The Lynx 4 SH represents a new leap forward in the field of slackline weblocks. A unique combination of innovative design, powerful mix of materials and top level production methods creating a weblock with leading performance.

Of particular note are the very low weight of less than 200 grams and the high strength of about 75 kN along with a highly efficient main diverter, utilizing the patented Evolve principle, and the generous side plate dimensions for secure webbing position.

name: Lynx 4.0 Vari
description:
The Lynx 4 variable version represents a new leap forward in the field of slackline weblocks. A unique combination of innovative design, powerful mix of materials and top level production methods creating a weblock with leading performance.

Of particular note are the very low weight of less than 230 grams and the high strength of about 70 kN along with a highly efficient main diverter, utilizing the patented Evolve principle, and the generous side plate dimensions for secure webbing position.

The Evolve diverter grants the gentle webbing fixation of a 36 mm diamter cylinder in extremely compact dimensions. The R-Lock pin securely protects the diverter against rotation. The Lynx 4 uses only corrosion-resistant materials such as anodized aerospace aluminium and high-strength stainless steel.

The variable version of the Lynx 4 features rearpin interface. With this design diverse connection and tensioning components can be attached directly to the Lynx 4 in fast "plug and play" manner. Thus, the Lynx 4 can be configured in a variety of setup situations. The direct attachment of our Soft-release system or the direct attachment of pulleys or rigging plates, using the ZenTube, is possible.

name: Mithril - Quick Pin
description: Aluminium weblock with 2 quick pins. Ideal for highline projects or for travels.

name: Orange
description: The Orange is a technological masterpiece with lots of functions which makes it the perfect highline weblock.

name: Paddle FX
description: Having a properly strung trickline is a must. If you are an enthusiastic trickliner who goes nuts every time you grab a ratchet, then grab a Paddle!

name: Paddle SH
description: World unique anchor tool for locking 50 mm trickline webbing. Adequate solution for rigging todays modern tricklines.

name: Pirat PP
description: Light, yet sufficiently strong allround 1-inch weblock. If you are looking for "all in one" solution for all your projects, throw Pirat in your backpack for your next adventure!

name: Pirat QP
description: Light, yet sufficiently strong allround 1-inch weblock. If you are looking for "all in one" solution for all your projects, throw Pirat in your backpack for your next adventure!

name: PRO Weblock
description: The PRO Weblock is the result of many years of development at raed slacklines. In this version we added all our technologies to equip you with the best weblock we can imagine.
notes: MBS from Raed's own page: 62 kN (Wayback 2021-22; the 2019 page said 75 kN). SlackDB listed 100 kN. The PRO Weblock X-Link was an X-Link variant of this weblock, sold alongside it in 2019.

name: Puma 2.0
description:
The Puma is our specially developed webbing anchor for professional jump- and tricklining, now in the 2. generation. We set a special focus on the very robust and yet lightweight design with the direct shackle interface.

The Puma is the ideal partner for hard workouts thanks to the high breaking load of more than 7 tons. The main diverter with 28 mm diameter gives a high break strength efiiciency of the jumpline webbing. The webbing can be quickly assembled and disassembled due to the pushbutton frontpin. More precise setup thanks to the ablity for pretightening the webbing belong to the standard repertoire of the Puma.

The highlights of the 2. generation are the direct shackle interface to VanBeest GreenPin shackles (2T and 1.5T modells), the frontpin made of high strength 17-4 PH stainless steel and the larger main diverter with roller lock.

name: RamLock
description: The SlackTech RamLock is the most advanced slackline weblock available to date. The RamLock is the first ever, low profile slackline weblock that has deviated from the standard, 19 year-old banana style design. Our goal with this slackline weblock was to create an incredibly strong, yet highly versatile 1 inch webbing anchor that any slacker can use regardless of their slackin' style.

name: Rhino Minion
description: The Rhino Minion is the mix breeding between the Rhino and Frog, both lightweight 281g and strong with its 60 kN MBS entirely in stainless steel hand welded and tested in independent laboratory. Moreover the Rhino Minion keeps a pin of 12 mm and a central diverter big enough to exploit the strength of the webbing up to 95% as with the Rhino. 100% Made in France

name: RhinoLock
description: The RhinoLock is super solid and built to last, this versatile webbing anchor is for those wanting to go longer!

name: RODEO Ultralight Weblock
description: You don't want any additional weight dangling around in your loose rodeoline. An incredible weight of merely 57 gram makes RODEO without any doubt the lightest fully functional weblock on the planet. And yet it's strong: With a MBS of 17 kN this weblock is precisely engineered for your surfy rodeo lines. The cnc milled 7075 aluminium body provides a high safety margin and a soft shackle attachment point allows for the lowest weighing setup ever. Of course it's easy to pretension too.
notes: The aluminium RODEO, introduced mid-2021: first on raed-slacklines.com/rodeo-weblock in the Wayback capture of 2021-07-25, announced on Raed's blog 2021-08-14 ("New RODEO weblock"). It replaced the RODEO Steel Weblock (#143) under the same URL; the Dec 2017 date this row used to carry was the steel one's launch.

unmodelled.full_name: Souz Slackline Rowan 1.0 Captive Pin Light

name: SeaHorse DP 1.5
description: The seaHorse is the world’s first ISA 51 certified HighTech Highline Weblock. Made from a single piece of aluminium, has a versatile HollowCenterDiverter and a excellent PreTension-Ability. This WebLock also impresses with its low weight and, at the same time, the generous dimensioning, which allows comfortable handling (even with up to 8mm thick slackline webbing).

name: Slackibloc 3.1
description: The weblocks allow to anchor your slackline webbing in an adjustable way and without decreasing its strength. Essential for longlines and Highlines. Smart and easy to use, the Slackiblock3 accept standard dimensions webbing up to 28mm wide and 10mm thickness. Economic release made from painted steel with stainless steel lockable pin.

name: Slackibloc Jump 1.2
description: Tensionable weblock for trickline and jumpline tension, closed around the webbing with a rotating plate and no moving parts. Two connection eyes: one to back up or to pull on pulleys, the second the eye it must be tensioned by when slacking. Takes flat polyester and polyamide webbing as standard, and a reinforced wrap around the large roller holds slippery webbing (Dyneema, Vectran) at the cost of adjustability.
notes: Specs from Slack Inov's own "Notice d'utilisation SLACKIBLOC JUMP" (5 pp., filed as the product's manual). This row and the row formerly at id 95 ("Slackijump") were two SlackDB scrapes of ONE product; 95 is removed and this row is the survivor, keeping the maker's "1.2" in the name. The manual settles which scrape described the hardware: it states 580 g and a rotating plate with two connection eyes, which is this row's 580 g, Rotatable Side Plates and Double Mounting Hole - 95 claimed 517 g, a captive pin and a single mounting hole. It also corrects BOTH scrapes on two figures. MBS is 80 kN per the manual; this row carried 95 kN and 95 carried 100 kN, and neither appears in the maker's own document. Compatible width is 30-52 mm: the manual gives 40-52 mm with no shims and 30-42 mm with two, so the range recorded here is the union of the two configurations, not a single quoted span - this row carried 24-51 mm and 95 carried 49-51 mm. The manual adds that connectors up to 20 mm diameter fit, and that thickness may be 0-10 mm in either configuration; the model has no column for either. date_introduced (Jul 2018) is carried over from 95, the only place it was recorded, and the manual does not contradict it. Price is this row's 60.00 EUR; 95 listed 65.00 EUR, and the manual quotes no price, so the cheaper of two undated scrapes of a product that is no longer sold is not a safe correction to make - both figures are recorded here.

unmodelled.full_name: Slack Inov Slackibloc SR Pull pin
Slack Inov Slackibloc SR Quick Pin

name: T-Rig
description: As successor of our trusted T-Lock, the T-Rig is even lighter and can be directly Installed into your pulley sastem. It consists of 30 mm/1” main roller made of pressure-resistant plastic that minimises reduction of the breaking strength of the webbing. The webbing is easily inserted, pretensioned and retightened due to a rotable and removable, yet unlosable, bolt.

name: TiLock 19mm - Titanium Pins
description: Titanium-framed push-pin weblock for 19mm webbing, in the titanium-PushPin configuration — the lighter and more expensive of the two pin options Raed offer.
notes: Manufacturer page (raed-sports.com/tilock): the TiLock is configured on order — webbing width 19mm or 25mm, and PushPins in high-strength steel or titanium. The titanium frame is the same in every configuration; only the pins differ. Steel-pin price is the listed base (129.95 EUR); titanium pins are the 229.95 EUR option. Held as four rows because a configuration that changes the price and the weight is a product, not a note on one.

name: TiLock 25mm - Titanium Pins
description: Titanium-framed push-pin weblock for 25mm webbing, in the titanium-PushPin configuration — the lighter and more expensive of the two pin options Raed offer.
notes: Manufacturer page (raed-sports.com/tilock): the TiLock is configured on order — webbing width 19mm or 25mm, and PushPins in high-strength steel or titanium. The titanium frame is the same in every configuration; only the pins differ. Steel-pin price is the listed base (129.95 EUR); titanium pins are the 229.95 EUR option. Held as four rows because a configuration that changes the price and the weight is a product, not a note on one.

name: Zilla 2.0
description:
Our Zilla 2.0 is the vigorous leader among the slackline anchor devices. The application range of the Zilla includes longlines over 100 meter up to 16 kN pretension. Despite its massive structure there isn´t any ounce too much. Weight and function optimization was one of our main goals.

The most striking feature of the Zilla 2.0 is the great and handy Quickpin, which allows a rapid fixation of the line. The possibility of pre-tightening the line with hand power gives great precision and efficiency when using a pulley tightening system. Thanks to the 36 mm diameter of the main deviator - the Zilla 2.0 defines a very high maximum breaking load factor.

name: Zilla 3.0
description:
The newly developed and completely revised 3rd generation of our high-tension weblock, the Zilla, comes up with new highlights and innovations. High-strength and ultra-robust structure was our main priority. The Zilla 3 is the worldwide leader in terms of breaking strength and also webbing strength reduction and is intended for very long longline projects and slackline rigs demanding a high degree of safety.

The most striking novelty is the middle diverter, realised with a new geometry for the webbing to wrap around. This Evolve -technology, registered for patent approval, allows us to maximise the breaking strength efficiency of the slackline while staying within minimal dimensions. This makes it possible to have a middle diverter with the efficiency of Ø60 mm using a smaller area than the previous Ø36 mm Zilla 2 diverter integrated in the device. The R-Lock-Design very efficiently prevents any rotation of the middle diverter under very high and sudden shockloads and thus minimises the danger of the slackline slipping under such extreme loads.

The direct fit to the compact and highly secure Green-Pin shackles ( 2to WLL and 3.25to WLL ) creates a consistently high safety standard and a high fatigue resistance in slackline anchors and tensioning systems. The spacious eyes at the back of the device (Versat Eye) allow for shackles to be passed through, so that the Zilla 3 can be positioned on the shackle bow. This is a great advantage in special rigging systems (9:1 interface, mounting to pulleys and rigging plates). The pin connecting the side-plates in the back prevents any nonlinear loading of the structure.

The large 4-ball-pushpin, made from high tensile and highly rigid stainless steel,facilitates a safe anchorage with high pull-out resistance. The Quick-release-concept allows for a fast installing and taking out of the webbing.

The generously spacious design of the side-plates excellently guides very thick webbing (e.g. threaded lines) or doubled up layers (Double layup training).

name: Slackfriend
description: Radrigs' lever-action weblock for rodeo lines and low-tension park lines. The locking mechanism uses no webbing-on-webbing friction, so pre-tensioning is easy and tension can be released in a controlled way by pulling the handle. The quoted 120 g includes the integrated Dyneema soft-shackle connector, so no extra hardware is needed.
notes: Manufacturer specs (radrigs.co.uk): 85 x 45 x 45 mm, 120 g incl. soft shackle, approved webbing width up to 26 mm, WLL 3 kN, MBS 20 kN. Centre diverter and ring 7075-T6 aluminium, side plates hard-anodised 6082-T6, soft shackle 5 mm SK78 Dyneema. Designed and manufactured in the UK. Width recorded as 26 mm because Radrigs publish only an upper bound, not a range. TYPE CORRECTED: listed as a roller/pulley in earlier sweeps — it is a weblock. Radrigs note that post-Brexit EU orders are routed through SlackX.eu.

name: MightyLock
description: High strength retention line-lock ring. The line-lock ring reinvented. The unique shape and geometry of the MightyLock give it unprecedented strength rentention with optimized fitting on shackle pins. Great for static ends, backups, and longlines!
notes: Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): MBS 42 kN, WLL 10 kN, 54.0 g. Inner length 26.0 mm, inner width 20.0 mm, height/thickness 12.0 mm. Anodised aluminium. 25 mm side pairs with the pin of a 12 mm bow shackle; 20 mm side with a 10 mm bow or 1/2" anchor shackle. Works on the bow side of most shackles. Catch cord is 2.75 mm Sterling GloCord. Colours: black, blue, orange, purple. No pin of its own — recorded as connection type Other. Date introduced is the Shopify listing publish date (2020-05-25).

name: Aluminum Line-Locker Ring
description: 1-inch aluminum line-locker ring. A drop-forged aluminum ring sized perfectly for building 1-inch line-lockers. Ideal for setting up line-lockers on carabiners or the bow-side of a shackle!
notes: Manufacturer specs (balancecommunity.com): MBS 15 kN, WLL 3 kN, drop-forged anodised aluminium alloy 6061. No weight published (the 91 g Shopify figure is shipping weight, not product weight) — left null. Date introduced is the Shopify listing publish date (2020-01-27).

name: ChainLock
description: A forged, green-anodised chain link sold as a cheap line-locker for rodeo lines and lines up to about 40 m, or as the multiplier connection in a HangOver pulley system. Explicitly not recommended for highlines, and it cannot pre-tension the webbing when used with a shackle or carabiner.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slacktivity.com): MBS 30 kN, WLL 6 kN, 23 g, forged 7075-T6 aluminium, green anodised. Outer 50 x 35 mm, inner 30 x 15 mm. Designed for 25 mm webbing; a separately sold 3D-printed spacer (bundled or standalone, €16.00 for the bundle) adapts it to 20 mm — hence the 20-25 mm range. Slacktivity's own note: low-tension setups up to 50 m only; the seaHorse is their recommendation above that. Price is the base ChainLock (€9.00).

name: ZENLOCK
description: Slack Inov's current flagship weblock: 200 g, 60 kN MBS, and adjustable from 17 to 26 mm webbing via screw-fixed rigid aluminium spacers that cannot be dropped. A large progressive spiral diverter preserves roughly 95 % of the webbing MBS and doubles as an auxiliary anchor point for a multiplier; a lowered front pin reduces friction damage. The rear becket accepts metallic and soft connectors, and a separate slot takes a soft release or 25 mm soft shackle directly.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slacklines.us / Slack Inov): 200 g, MBS 60 kN, 17-26 mm webbing. Spacer configuration: none for 24-26 mm, one pair (included) for 19-23 mm, two pairs (sold separately) for 15-17 mm. Stainless steel safety pin with double-action (press + pull) unlock and fall-arrest cord; reinforced anodised aluminium head; included round-head allen key. Sold with optional 7 m/13 m soft release and 0.3 T Dyneema sling; base price is the bare weblock. BRAND: sold on slacklines.us under the 'Spider Slackline US' vendor field, but the product is Slack Inov's (its own press photography is filed as 'slackinov') — filed under the true maker per the retailer rule. Date introduced is the Shopify listing publish date (2025-11-12).

name: Diamond Lock
description: A diamond/square-section locker ring offered as a lighter, part-free alternative to a weblock. Slack Inov pitch it as a replacement for a frost knot on highline backup webbing, for primitive park setups, and as a static longline end blocker on webbing without end loops. Unlike some ascender-style locks it is designed to retain around 85 % of the webbing strength.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slacklines.us data sheet): 54 g (1.9 oz), ring thickness 12 mm (0.47 in), WLL 10 kN, MBS 40 kN. Square shape: the 1-inch side takes the pin of a standard 1-inch shackle, the 20 mm side the pin of a standard 10 mm shackle. Compatible with 17-20 mm backup webbing and 24-26 mm webbing — recorded as a 17-26 mm range. BRAND: the shop's own vendor field reads SLACK-INOV', not Spider — filed under the true maker per the retailer rule. Colours: light blue, red. Shopify publish date 2024-06-14 is a bulk store migration, not a release date, so date_introduced is left null.

name: Blueberry SR
description: The soft-release variant of the Blueberry: the same tempered-aluminium body, plus a second bottom pin so a soft release or a sling can enter the weblock directly, removing one connector from the anchor. The anodised aluminium diverter retains about 95 % of the webbing's resistance and the stainless pins let the webbing slide freely while tensioning.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slacklines.us data sheet): 125 g (4.41 oz), WLL 10 kN, MBS 48 kN, for 24-26 mm polyester or nylon webbing up to 10 mm thick. Push-button stainless/aluminium head requiring a double movement to unlock, with an anti-drop mini sling. Suggested connector: 2.2 T stainless bow shackle. Sold with optional 7 m/13 m soft release and 0.3 T Dyneema sling; base price is the bare weblock. Spider warn it is not PPE. Shopify publish date 2024-06-14 is a bulk store migration, not a release date, so date_introduced is left null.

name: Blueberry
description: A light, robust 1-inch weblock built around a tempered-aluminium body with an anodised aluminium diverter that spreads load across the webbing surface. The stainless steel pin slides freely during setup, the push button needs a press-and-pull double movement to unlock, and a fall-arrest cord is included. The rear hole takes any standard connector.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slacklines.us data sheet): 165 g (5.82 oz), WLL 10 kN, MBS 48 kN, for 24-26 mm polyester or nylon webbing up to 10 mm thick. Suggested connector: 2.2 T (4,850 lb) stainless bow shackle. Optional 0.3 T Dyneema sling turns the diverter into a Buckingham tensioning system with Spider's ROLLEX. Spider warn it is not PPE and that a loose tail can derail in wind — always tie an anti-slip knot. Shopify publish date 2024-06-14 is a bulk store migration, not a release date, so date_introduced is left null.

name: Linelock Aluminum Ring
description: Spider's simplest webbing anchor — a forged, lime-green aluminium ring for locking webbing onto an oval-section connector. Recommended with an oval screw-gate steel carabiner to build a primitive pulley tensioning system.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slacklines.us data sheet): 20 g (0.71 oz), WLL 6 kN, MBS 30 kN, forged aluminium, lime green. Outer dimension 30 x 15 mm. For 24-26 mm polyester and nylon webbing, 1-5 mm thick; Spider note it also suits their JUMBO. Shopify publish date 2024-06-14 is a bulk store migration, not a release date, so date_introduced is left null.

name: Simplex Locker
description: A minimalist rectangular locking ring: the shape lets you pick the inner width to match your webbing (~20 mm or ~25 mm) for optimal locking geometry, retaining more than 80 % of the webbing's original strength. Single-wrap locks in one direction while still allowing pre-tensioning the other way; a double wrap all but eliminates slippage.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slackhouseshop.pl): MBS 36 kN, WLL 6 kN, 40 g, aluminium, 48 x 44 x 12 mm, inside width 21 / 26 mm. Made in Poland. Works best mounted directly to a shackle, preferably 'Kingpin' style — 12 mm shackle for ~25 mm webbing, 10 mm for ~20 mm. BRAND: sold by Slackhouse but the shop lists Petram as the producer — filed under the true maker per the retailer rule.

name: Weblock 50mm
description: Bera's 50 mm trickline weblock, in anodised blue aluminium with 6 mm side plates and a removable stainless steel pin secured by two ball detents. Sold bundled with a 5 m 'Street Balance' printed 50 mm webbing and a 50 mm soft release.
notes: Manufacturer specs (beraadventure.com.br): anodised aluminium, plate thickness 6 mm, overall width 63 mm, inner width 51 mm, length 145 mm, height 70 mm, WLL 10 kN, 600 g, blue. Removable stainless steel pin with two ball locks. No MBS published — left null. Price (R$399.00) is for the bundle: weblock + 5 m 50 mm webbing + 50 mm soft release, so it overstates the weblock alone.

name: Anel Linelock
description: A high-strength aluminium locking ring from Bera. The generous internal space is deliberate: it leaves room for a protective sleeve over the webbing, which is why Bera recommend it for locking off primitive systems.
notes: Manufacturer specs (beraadventure.com.br): breaking load 47 kN, working load 15 kN, high-strength aluminium, silver, 43 g. Stock diameter 12 mm, inner length 33 mm, outer length 58 mm. Listed out of stock at the time of import but still catalogued, so active is true.

name: Line Lock
description: The aluminium line lock used on the YogaSlackers eLine, also sold on its own as a replacement. It creates a movable, impermanent anchor anywhere along the line while retaining over 70 % of the webbing's strength — against roughly 60 % for a knot.
notes: Manufacturer specs (yogaslackers.com): material aluminium; no weight, MBS or dimensions published — left null. Sized for the 25 mm eLine. YogaSlackers advise clipping it to the carabiner on uninstall so it is not lost.

name: lineLoose Buckle
description: A buckle assembly for building a dedicated webbing de-tensioning (lineLoose) system with 24-32 mm webbing. Compared with improvising the same system on a shackle it adds an integrated 'weblock method' fixation for the loose end, and — more importantly — moves the inner end knot onto its own bar so the moving webbing never rubs over the knot, which is where that setup normally wears dangerously.
notes: Manufacturer specs (linegrip.com): SWL 10 kN, max allowable load 15 kN, MBS 45 kN, 430 g incl. delta links and pin, inside width 32 mm, approved webbing width 24-32 mm, buckle 103 x 10 x 55 mm, zinc-plated steel. In the box: buckle with spacer, 2x 8 mm delta link, 1x locker pin; webbing not included (10-20 m needed to wrap the release loops). Sold by lineGrip as a slackPro! last-stock sell-off under 'Discontinued Products' — hence active: false. Price is the net sell-off price (€30.00, ex VAT; was €42.10). Brand recorded as 'Slack Pro!', which canonical_brand() maps to 'lineGrip (formerly Slack Pro!)'.

name: Boa Constrictor
description: Viper's high-tension weblock, the result of four years of development. It pre-tensions easily, pairs with their slow release to hold tension by friction, and uses a captured pin so nothing can be dropped or left behind. For longer lines Viper pair it with their Grippex and Rolley in a Buckingham 3:1.
notes: Manufacturer specs (viperslacklines.co.za): 343 g, for 25 mm webbing. Hard-anodised gold aluminium diverter, powder-coated and laser-etched stainless steel side plates, stainless steel pins. No MBS published — left null. Date introduced is the Shopify listing publish date (2026-06-22), consistent with the 'proud to present' launch copy.

name: Aluminium Static Linelock Ring
description: A forged, anodised aluminium locking ring for low- to medium-tension 25 mm webbing. Combined with an oval carabiner or the bow side of a slackline shackle it makes a light, easy webbing lock — Viper aim it at rodeo lines, surf lines and classic lightweight primitive setups.
notes: Manufacturer specs (viperslacklines.co.za): MBS 25 kN, 37 g, overall size 60 mm, internal diameter 40 mm, forged anodised aluminium. Date introduced is the Shopify listing publish date (2025-11-03).

name: Viper Constrictor 25mm
description: A stainless steel linelock made in South Africa, used together with a slackline shackle to lock 25 mm webbing off to an anchor sling when the webbing has no sewn loop. Viper position their simpler aluminium ring as the cheaper option for short primitive lines and rodeo lines.
notes: Manufacturer specs (viperslacklines.co.za): stainless steel, for 25 mm / 1-inch webbing. No weight or MBS published — left null. Sold either as the locking pin alone (R225.00, recorded here) or bundled with a slackline shackle (R435.00). Date introduced is the Shopify listing publish date (2021-09-09).

name: Chainlink LineLocker
description: SlackGear's budget stainless steel line-locker for anchoring 25 mm webbing. Smooth-finished and intended for short or low-tension lines, used with a carabiner for quick setup.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slackgear.co.za): stainless steel, 60 g, for 25 mm (1-inch) webbing. No MBS published — left null.

name: Meercat LineLocker
description: A lightweight all-stainless webbing anchor for 25 mm webbing, rated by SlackGear for lines up to 100 m or 10 kN of pre-tension. The 14 mm main diverter behaves like a 19 mm equivalent, keeping it non-damaging to the webbing, and the geometry gives a twist-free connection to a safety cord.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slackgear.co.za): 100 % stainless steel, 95 g, 14 mm main diverter (19 mm effective equivalent), for lines up to 100 m or 10 kN pre-tension — recorded as WLL 10 kN. Best paired with a 12 mm stainless bow or D-shackle. No MBS published — left null.

name: Linelocker 50mm
description: A galvanised bent-steel hook for shortening thick 50 mm slacklines. Slackliner.de's argument against the usual chain-link method is that the hook lets the webbing clamp against itself rather than being crushed, which is gentler on the band and costs less breaking strength.
notes: Manufacturer specs (slackliner.de): galvanised bent steel, 12 mm stock, 15 mm centre bar, 480 g, for webbing up to 50 mm of any thickness. Shipping weight 0.48 kg. Slackliner.de state 'belastbar bis 5000 kg' (~49 kN) — that is a load rating of unstated type, not a published MBS, so breaking_strength is left null rather than guessed.

name: TiLock 19mm - Steel Pins
description: Titanium-framed push-pin weblock for 19mm webbing, in the high-strength-steel PushPin configuration — heavier than the titanium pins, and considerably cheaper.
notes: Manufacturer page (raed-sports.com/tilock): the TiLock is configured on order — webbing width 19mm or 25mm, and PushPins in high-strength steel or titanium. The titanium frame is the same in every configuration; only the pins differ. Steel-pin price is the listed base (129.95 EUR); titanium pins are the 229.95 EUR option. Held as four rows because a configuration that changes the price and the weight is a product, not a note on one.

name: TiLock 25mm - Steel Pins
description: Titanium-framed push-pin weblock for 25mm webbing, in the high-strength-steel PushPin configuration — heavier than the titanium pins, and considerably cheaper.
notes: Manufacturer page (raed-sports.com/tilock): the TiLock is configured on order — webbing width 19mm or 25mm, and PushPins in high-strength steel or titanium. The titanium frame is the same in every configuration; only the pins differ. Steel-pin price is the listed base (129.95 EUR); titanium pins are the 229.95 EUR option. Held as four rows because a configuration that changes the price and the weight is a product, not a note on one.

name: RigLock
description: Raed's most versatile weblock: a BLNC weblock and a rigging plate in one body, so the line can be tensioned directly off the lock. Steel frame with a large hollow aluminium diverter, a 17-4 PH steel Quick Lock PushPin, oversized holes for shackling under awkward rigging, and the SLIP LOCK anti-slippage feature that stops webbing creeping out under bounces and leash falls.
notes: Specs from the archived manufacturer page (web.archive.org capture of raed-slacklines.com/riglock, 2021-06-12). That page states the 62 kN breaking strength and ~95% webbing efficiency; the 10 kN WLL is read off the product label in Raed's own photo. Weight and diverter diameter are published nowhere we can source, and the webbing width is inherited from the PRO Weblock the page says it is built on — Raed also listed a 19mm RigLock separately.

name: SladLock Light
description: The light, minimal version of Slack.fr's SladLock — a self-blocking 25mm webbing lock for low-tension lines, taking up slack to set line length without a ratchet. Rated to a 5 kN working load only: Slack.fr rule out highline, trickline, pulley systems and lines over 50 m, pointing those at the SladLock Power or a banana instead.
notes: Specs from the archived shop page (web.archive.org captures of laboutique.slack.fr/282-sladlock-light.html, 2020-09-30 and 2022-09-30): Zicral 7075 alloy with SS 304 stainless, 5 kN WLL / 16 kN MBS, 135 g, 16 mm internal locking radius, captive pin. Price is 19.90 EUR incl. French VAT — the page displays 16.58 EUR ex-VAT, with no active reduction. Slack.fr warn that the laser marking on the part reads 18 kN, which is wrong: the breaking strength is 16 kN. Slack.fr later re-listed the same product as the "Mini Sladlock"; the URL, the laser marking and the product photo all still say Sladlock Light.

name: Alpine WebLock 6.2
description: Our general purpose webbing anchor, refined. The next iteration of the Alpine WebLock 6: full diverter sidewalls, a round front pin that spins while you tension, and a pin parking spot so it never drops mid-rig.
notes: Specs from the manufacturer's product page (balancecommunity.com, read 2026-09-24): 7075 anodized aluminium body, 17-4 PH stainless pin with a 2024 aluminium handle and 440C stainless locking balls; 60 kN MBS / 12 kN WLL (5:1 design factor); upper becket 56 kN MBS / 8 kN WLL, lower becket 70 kN MBS / 10 kN WLL; 24-26 mm webbing, 20 mm webbing only with the Alpine Weblock Spacers (Balance list the Axiom, Axiom MK2 and Silk 99 as not compatible). 242 g; 126.0 x 74.2 mm, 44.2 mm body thickness, 12 mm pin. Date introduced is the store listing date (2026-09-13). Price 125.10 USD.

unmodelled.full_name: Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters Alpine WebLock 6.2

name: Alpine WebLock 6.2 - Double Pin
description: Two pins, one weblock. The Alpine WebLock 6.2 with a second quick pin at the rear, for direct attachment to slings, soft shackles and soft releases — same diverter, same beckets, same strength.
notes: Specs from the manufacturer's product page (balancecommunity.com, read 2026-09-24): 7075 anodized aluminium body, 17-4 PH stainless pin with a 2024 aluminium handle and 440C stainless locking balls; 60 kN MBS / 12 kN WLL (5:1 design factor); upper becket 56 kN MBS / 8 kN WLL, lower becket 70 kN MBS / 10 kN WLL; 24-26 mm webbing, 20 mm webbing only with the Alpine Weblock Spacers (Balance list the Axiom, Axiom MK2 and Silk 99 as not compatible). 278 g; 123.6 x 71.2 mm, 44.2 mm body thickness, 12 mm pins. Date introduced is the store listing date (2026-09-17). Price 125.10 USD.

unmodelled.full_name: Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters Alpine WebLock 6.2 - Double Pin

name: Raptor
description: The Raptor is a slackline webbing locker with an ultra light weight (133 g), a large breaking strength (68 kN) and a wide range of connection options with a focus on textile elements, especially soft shackles.
notes: Specs from the manufacturer's shop page (Wayback copy of 2025-08-14, in stock then at 124.95 EUR) and the Raptor manual Rev 1.0: one-piece CNC body of 7075 T651 aluminium, 17-4 PH stainless front and rear push pins (9.5 mm), hollow main diverter tapering from 30 mm to 18 mm; 24.5-26 mm webbing, max. 3 mm thick; 10 kN WLL; 133 g; 99 x 52 x 71 mm. MBS is the manual's 64 kN (3 sigma, ISA test method), which the shop's spec list repeats — the body engraving and the shop blurb say 68 kN. The rear interface takes soft shackles, soft releases, 0.5-1 t spansets, two strands of rope, 10/12 mm shackles and 8/10 mm quicklinks; the manual does not approve carabiners for highline use. Made in Germany, Taiwan and China. Aki's shop is behind a password page as of 2026-10-05.

name: Slackibloc Slim SR
description: The SLACKIBLOC Slim is a light and strong weblock, ideal for any thin webbing. It is almost the same than Slackibloc SR with Soft Release option but thinnest for high end webbings.
notes: Specs from the Spider Slacklines shop page (product 458, ref. LLILR; Wayback copies of 2021-09-15 in English and 2022-05-24 in Italian), which is the same listing as Slack Inov's own shop. The narrow version of the Slackibloc SR, for 17-22 mm webbing up to 10 mm thick (not compatible with standard 25 mm webbing); accepts 1.5 wraps for slippery Dyneema webbing. 4 mm tempered aluminium plates, anodized aluminium hollow diverter (30 mm), stainless steel pins; front pin either the CLASSIC quick-lock pin or the SAFETY push pin; the rear pin takes a soft release directly. The page contradicts itself on two figures. Weight: 163 g in the product's spec list, 173 g in the feature table and the prose (173 g is also the standard SR's weight); 163 g recorded. MBS: 50 kN in the English feature table and engraved on the product photos, 60 kN in the Italian feature table and 'above 60 kN' in the prose; 50 kN recorded. WLL is 15 kN in both feature tables but the photos are engraved 10 kN. Price 89.95 EUR (English page, 2021); the Italian page showed 81.93 EUR in 2022. Date introduced is the shop listing date (2021-05-12). Still listed in Wayback captures of 2023; current status unknown, since both shops refuse automated requests.

name: Alpine WebLock 3.0
description: A new standard for webbing anchors. Beautiful two piece design with extremely versatile anchor hole. Rounded edges everywhere to protect your precious webbing, and a ultra high-strength front pin. The most advanced webbing anchor on the market.
notes: Specs from the manufacturer's shop page (balancecommunity.com, Wayback capture of 2014-06-10; the page was also captured at /alpine-weblock-30 from 2013-02 to 2015-03). Two-piece body machined from solid aluminium blocks, so the centre diverter is fixed and cannot rotate. 60 kN MBS / 12 kN WLL (5:1); 332 g; 120.6 x 61.9 x 44.5 mm; approved for 1" (25 mm) webbing. Quick-release front pin: 17-4 PH stainless steel, 2024 aluminium handle, four 440C stainless locking balls, 12.7 mm diameter, 38 mm long, 164.1 kN double-shear and 10.3 kN pull-out strength. The anchor hole takes a 7/16" or 1/2" bow shackle, the Van Beest 5/8" bolt-type shackle, or an oval / modified-D carabiner. Strength retention 90.2% with Balance Community Mantra MKIII (37.8 kN); recorded as the efficiency. Made in the USA. Price 119.95 USD (114.95 each for 2, 109.95 each for 4). Succeeded by the Alpine WebLock 4.0.

unmodelled.full_name: Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters Alpine WebLock 3.0

name: Alpine WebLock 2.2
description: The Alpine WebLock 2.2 (AWL2.2) is the next generation webbing anchor. With a super light construction that is stronger than nearly any slackline webbing on the market, the AWL2.2 is the perfect webbing anchor for all dedicated slackliners. Never before has such a small device been so useful in slacklining.
notes: Specs from the manufacturer's shop page (balancecommunity.com, Wayback capture of 2012-08-01; SKU AN-AWL2.2). Sideplates 1/8" alloy 4130 steel, powder-coated black; diverter 6061-T6 aluminium, anodized green, 28.6 mm (1-1/8") diameter, 1-1/32" wide. 576 g total, which includes the 7/16" forged 316 stainless bow shackle that comes fitted as the anchor connection (15,500 lbf); 57 kN MBS / 12 kN WLL; 6-1/2 x 2-1/4 x 3 in. Approved webbing widths 15/16" to 1-1/16" (about 24-27 mm). Quick-release front pin: 4130 steel, aluminium handle, 12.7 mm (1/2") diameter, 32,800 lbf double shear, 1,160 lbf pull-out. Strength retention: polyester webbings keep at least 93% and nylon at least 98% of their rating; 93% recorded as the efficiency. An optional RAGElock Conversion Kit (19.95 USD) converts it to 1.25" webbing. Made in Sacramento, CA. Price 119.95 USD. Successor of the Alpine WebLock 2.0, succeeded by the 3.0.

unmodelled.full_name: Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters Alpine WebLock 2.2

name: MONSTER Lock
description: The MONSTER LOCK is the grand supreme webbing anchor. With a gigantic 3.25" diameter diverter, this device will hold 99.999% of the strength of all 1" webbings (including Spider Silk MKII).
notes: Specs from the manufacturer's shop page (balancecommunity.com, Wayback capture of 2012-07-10; SKU AN-ML; captured from 2012-07 to 2013-07). A large wrap-around roller (82.55 mm / 3.25" diameter, 26.19 mm inner width) CNC-milled from two blocks of 6061-T6 aluminium, anodized green and joined by three alloy steel shoulder bolts; sideplates 1/4" alloy 4130 steel, laser cut, bent and powder-coated black. 1,280 g; 100 kN MBS / 25 kN WLL; 7-1/8 x 4-13/16 x 3-3/4 in. Approved webbing widths 15/16" to 1-1/16". The webbing runs around the roller to a centre bolt, with three modes: zero wraps (adjusting only, holds no tension), one wrap (adjustable in one direction, slips at 31 kN) and two wraps (locked, 99.999% strength retention, recorded as 100%). The sideplates bolt directly to SMC 3" double pulleys with the included grade-8 bolts (bent inwards for a 5:1, outwards for a 9:1), and the static side takes a 5/8" or 3/4" anchor shackle (optimised for the Van Beest 5/8" bolt-type). Made in Sacramento, CA. Price 259.95 USD as a standalone; the bolt option added 10 USD and the shackle option 20 USD. None of the shop's product photos survive in the Wayback Machine; the two photos are user-supplied.

unmodelled.full_name: Balance Community: Slackline Outfitters MONSTER Lock

name: Lockman
description: This unique pin is made from fine stainless steel and produced in small batches. The dumbbell shape gives a 25mm/1 inch slackline a safe position and guarantees a damage free fixation. The setup of the anchor is really fast and comfortable. The Lockman is fasten via a cord to the shackle. Thus the Lockman won´t get lost. Its really an ideal tool for anchoring slacklines without sewn loop.
notes: A dumbbell-shaped stainless pin that sits inside a shackle (23–26 mm mouth only, straight or bow, no carabiners or quicklinks) — the shackle is the weblock body, so pin/attachment types are recorded as Other. Maker's page (Wayback 2014-12-31, English; German 2013-03-18 capture agrees): inner width 26 mm, overall 52 mm, 12 mm roller, WLL 10 kN, strength >30 kN, 75 g, cord and side fixing screw, in use since 2008, made in Saxony. 16.95 € solo (26.50 / 28.50 € with a straight / bow 12 mm HW shackle). Manual rev 1.1 (German): 25 mm webbing up to 3.5 mm thick, not for highlines, max. rigging height 2 m, max. 10 kN; webbing strength depends on the line (e.g. new White Magic ≈23 kN).

name: Lockman 2.0
description: This unique pin is made from fine stainless steel and produced in small batches. The dumbbell shape gives a 25mm/1 inch slackline a safe position and guarantees a damage free fixation. The setup of the anchor is really fast and comfortable. For the 2nd generation, we have the Lockman designed a little longer and added an elastic catch cord including a practical attachment notch. The Lockman 2.0 can be easily fixed to the shackle. The attached slackline is also held in position by the cord. This results in a significant gain regarding handling and safety.
notes: Made by Landcruising; Aki Slacklines sold the same product as 'Aki Lockman 2' (16.50 €, Wayback 2021-07-28: https://web.archive.org/web/20210728193156/https://aki-slacklines.de/de/hardware/bandhalter/13/aki-lockman-2-bandhalter?c=13), so this is one row with Aki as a seller. Maker's page (Wayback 2016-11-03, same as 2016-10-07): longer than the first Lockman, with an elastic catch cord and attachment notch; inner width 26 mm, overall 64 mm, 12 mm roller, WLL 8 kN, strength >30 kN, 93 g, made in Saxony; Aki's page adds 64 x 18 x 18 mm and CNC-turned. Shackles of 23–26 mm mouth only. 16.95 € solo. The page links its own English manual ('Manual-Lockman 2.0', lockman2-manual-rev1.1-eng-web.pdf), which was never archived; Aki's German manual Rev. 1.2 is held instead: https://web.archive.org/web/20240703082000/https://aki-slacklines.de/media/pdf/7c/17/2c/lockman2-manual-rev12-web-deu.pdf

name: Puma 32
description: The Puma is our dedicated jumpline webbing anchor for the professionals. We set the focus on a super sturdy approach with direct shackle interface and a lightweight and powerful design. Thanks to the high breaking strength of nearly 6 tons it is possible to rig and work out high tension lines with a sufficient safety margin. The big diameter of the main roller ensures a high efficiency of the webbing strength, specially for polyamide lines. The quick locking pin enables the fast setup and remove of the line. Precise rigging due to the possibility of hand adjustation before tightening is a standard task for the Puma.
notes: First-generation Puma (Puma 2.0 is #66), a jumpline weblock for 30–32 mm webbing incl. threaded tubular. Maker's page (Wayback 2012-08-22): Ø15 mm galvanized-steel quick-lock front pin, Ø24 mm 7075 aluminium main roller, 4 mm stainless side plates, M12 10.9 steel screws, direct shackle interface up to 15 mm bolt, 380 g solo, WLL 14 kN, metal body >59 kN, 43.5 kN tested with Matrix webbing; not for Dyneema or Dyneema-hybrid webbing. Made in Saxony. 69.95 € solo, 79.95 € with a 13 mm stainless shackle. The page links a manual whose link was not archived; the manual is held instead from Aki's "Puma 1" product archive (2012, filed as Product archive), whose second page is the Puma 32 manual Rev. 1.0: https://web.archive.org/web/20220517052335/https://aki-slacklines.de/media/pdf/a9/48/98/product-archive-puma1.pdf Part of the Puma jumpline webbing anchor series: Puma 26, 35 and 50 versions (for 26, 35 and 50 mm webbing) were available on request, per the series photo; they are recorded here, not as rows of their own.

name: BLNC Weblock
description: The BLNC Weblock is a true working horse weblock. It provides all the best features known from our PRO weblock, like a big hollow diverter, a pushpin at the front, strong steel construction and easy pretensioning. But instead of a second PushPin it comes with really big holes for easiest attaching of a shackle even under difficult rigging circumstances.
notes: Maker's page (Wayback 2019-08-26 to 2021-11-26, English): steel frame, large hollow aluminium diverter on three steel axes, one 17-4 PH Quick Lock PushPin at the front and big holes instead of a second pin, for a shackle. 25 mm webbing. MBS 50 kN and 284 g on the 2019 page, 62 kN on the 2021 one (weight no longer listed); WLL 10 kN is read off the label in the maker's photo. 89.95 € throughout. Gone after 2021, when the RigLock (#130, "a BLNC weblock and a rigging plate in one body") took its place; Raed's Beginner Longline Set page still names it in 2025.

name: RODEO Steel Weblock
description: You don't want any additional weight dangling around in your loose rodeoline. That's why the ultralight RODEO weblock definitely contains more air than metal. An incredible weight of merely 136 gram makes this without any doubt the lightest fully functional weblock on the planet. And yet it's strong: With a MBS of 13 kN this weblock is precisely engineered for your surfy rodeo lines. ROCsolid steel provides a high safety margin and a huge hollowtech center diverter preserves the strength of your webbing. Of course it's easy to pretension too. So what are you waiting for? Go lightweight and surf BIIIG!
notes: The first RODEO, before the aluminium RODEO Ultralight Weblock (#73), which replaced it under the same URL in mid-2021. A ROCsolid steel frame with a hollowtech diverter. Launched at 114 g / MBS 9 kN (Wayback 2019-01-25: "preorders available now, shipping starts end of January 2018", 59.95 €). Redesigned in June 2019 (Raed's blog, 2019-06-13: smoother pretensioning, ball lock pin, higher webbing guidance, more strength) to 136 g, WLL 4 kN, MBS 13 kN, "prohibited for tricklining and highlining". Sold at 59.95 € (later 79.95 € marked down to 59.95 €) until the last steel capture, 2021-01-17, out of stock. The specs here are the 2019 redesign's.

name: PRO Weblock X-Link
description: The PRO weblock is the perfect compagnon to our PRO pulley system. It doesn't need any shackle. Attach it directly to an ultralight Dyneema whoopie sling and you have a perfect slackline anchor. The hollowtech center diverter makes this masterpiece of engineering one of the lightest anchorpoints in the market. And with a MBS of 75 kN it is extremely strong.
notes: A version of the PRO Weblock #65 with the X-Link anchor of the PRO pulley system, which takes a Dyneema whoopie sling directly with no shackle (patented, per the page). From its own page (Wayback 2019-01-25 to 2019-11-20, English and German): hollowtech centre diverter, 389 g, 109 €; that page gave MBS 75 kN, set here to #65's 62 kN like #65 itself. Material, WLL, pin types, webbing width, diverter and usage are #65's, which this page does not state.
